Consult Summary:
- 35-year-old female with a 3-day history of severe diarrhea, vomiting, and fever, unresponsive to oral rehydration salts.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe diarrhea (initially watery, now loose) for 3 days, associated with fever and vomiting.
- Frequency: At least 4 times/day today; exact number not recalled.
- Vomiting: Unable to retain any fluids or food; last episode approx. 2 hours ago.
- Fever: Feels very hot, subjective only (no measured temperature).
- Abdominal pain: Soreness centered around the navel; pain comes and goes, especially before urge to pass stool.
- Urination: Last passed urine approximately 1 hour ago; unable to comment on urine color; passing urine normally.
- No blood in stool or urine.
- No rash or other associated symptoms.
- No recent travel. Brother has had similar symptoms (“everyone in school has this”); recent contact.
- Bowel habits normally regular; no prior episodes of diarrhea or constipation.
- Past medical history: No history of abdominal problems or surgeries. Occasional menstrual cramps.
- Medications: Daily vitamin D; occasional ibuprofen for menstrual pain (“dose/route/frequency not documented”).
- Allergies: Not mentioned.
- Social: Non-smoker, occasional alcohol. Lives with mother and brother. Occupation: graphic designer. Working from home due to illness.
- Preventive care: Not mentioned.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented.
- Physical findings: Not documented.

Impression:
- Likely infectious gastroenteritis (possibly viral; bacterial etiology to be ruled out given severity and lack of improvement).

Plan:
- Continue oral rehydration salts, taking in tiny, frequent sips.
- Simple diet advised: toast, biscuit, bland foods; avoid fruit, vegetables, milk.
- Arrange urgent clinic appointment for clinical assessment of hydration and stool sample for testing.
- Monitor for worsening symptoms, especially inability to keep fluids down or deterioration—advise to attend A&E if this occurs.
- Contact support line to book urgent appointment.

Quality checks:
●	Missing: Allergies, full medication list/reconciliation, baseline health status, recent weight, specific assessment of hydration on examination.
●	Internal conflicts: None identified.
●	Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; all major clinical fields addressed except allergies/medication details.
